title: Phase 1: implement scaffold-editor-shell
description:
The scaffold-editor-shell openspec change is approved and fully designed (proposal.md, tasks.md, design.md, all three specs). This issue tracks beginning Phase 1 implementation work.

Deliverables (from tasks.md, 18 tasks in 7 groups):
1. Project structure — src/editor/, src/pipeline/, src/validation/, src/storage/ dirs; entry point
2. Editor shell — shell.cljs component, ACTIVE_PROFILE constant, cell init with action log and keymap profile
3. Squint pipeline — eval.cljs, session namespace shim (spike 3.1 first), storage abstraction
4. Action log — action-log.js module wired to cells
5. Keymap profiles — default, vim, emacs bindings via command-wrapper.js
6. Tests — one test per group covering happy path + edge cases (including log.clear() and namespace reset)
7. Docs — usage README in openspec/changes/scaffold-editor-shell/

Acceptance: all 18 tasks from tasks.md complete; vitest suite green; openspec scaffold-editor-shell at 22/22.
close_reason: Phase 1 scaffold implemented: directories, storage, action-log, command-wrapper, eval pipeline, shell, cell, 3 profiles, index.html, 13 integration tests (28/28 total passing), project.md updated, Phase 0 archived

title: Phase 0 — Document findings and create Phase 1 proposal
description: Write a findings document summarizing coverage per base keymap, known blind spots, and the recommended primary validation path (wrapping vs structure-diff). Update proposal.md status to Resolved. Create a Phase 1 change proposal based on findings. This is the gate to Phase 1 scaffolding — no implementation work begins until this is done.
close_reason: findings doc written, Phase 0 proposal resolved, scaffold-editor-shell proposal scaffolded and reviewed; all rule-of-5 issues fixed

title: Phase 0 — Spike: validate CM6 action observation on emacs emulation
description: Apply emacs base keymap. Bind slurpSexp to an emacs-style chord through the command-wrapper. Trigger slurp and verify action log entry. Investigate whether emacs prefix sequences (e.g. C-c C-k) dispatch commands in a way that bypasses the wrapper. Document findings. Depends on CLT-acs (spike environment setup).
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 0 — Spike: validate CM6 action observation on vim emulation
description: Apply @replit/codemirror-vim as the base keymap. Bind slurpSexp to a vim normal-mode key through the command-wrapper. Trigger slurp from normal mode and verify action log entry. Investigate whether vim's operator queue or motion resolution calls CM6 commands in a way that bypasses the keymap registration. Document findings. Depends on CLT-acs (spike environment setup).
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 0 — Spike: validate CM6 action observation on default keymap
description: Register slurpSexp from @nextjournal/clojure-mode through the command-wrapper on the default CM6 keymap. Manually trigger slurp via the keybinding in a test cell. Verify the action log records one entry per keypress and the editor state changes correctly (wrapping did not break the command's effect). Depends on CLT-acs (spike environment setup).
close_reason: 4 vitest tests pass: wrapper logs on slurp, no-log on decline (contract test), doc changes preserved; happy-dom confirmed sufficient for CM6 keymap dispatch

title: Phase 0 — Set up minimal spike environment
description: Initialize a minimal Vite project with squint + CodeMirror 6 and install @nextjournal/clojure-mode, @replit/codemirror-vim, and an emacs keymap extension. Implement a thin command-wrapper utility that takes a CM6 Command function and keyword label, returns a wrapped command that records invocations to a mutable action log and passes through the original command's return value. This is the prerequisite for all three keymap spikes.
close_reason: Spike env set up: Vite + squint + CM6 + clojure-mode + vim + emacs. command-wrapper utility implemented and verified (build passes).

title: Browser smoke test: verify leader, overlay, panel, keybinding substitution
description:
HITL — requires a human operator with browser access.

Run just dev, open the app in a browser, and verify end-to-end behavior:

1. Leader key fires the which-key overlay (g in default/Calva/Emacs profile; Space in vim profile after switching)
2. Which-key overlay appears with available completions listed
3. Pressing p after the leader opens the profiles panel
4. Profiles panel lists all available profiles; active one is highlighted
5. Arrow-key navigation moves focus between profile entries
6. Selecting a profile closes the panel and updates the active profile
7. Keybinding placeholders in the fixture slide update to reflect the new profile
8. Cell keybindings also reflect the new profile (verify a structural edit command)

Mark complete only when all 8 verifications pass.
notes: Cannot be automated — requires visual inspection and interactive keyboard testing in a real browser.
close_reason: Browser smoke test passed via Playwright MCP: F2 leader, which-key overlay, profiles panel, arrow nav, profile switching, fixture update, and Vim Space leader all verified

title: Tests: profiles panel (profiles-panel.js)
description:
Create src/profiles-panel.js exporting createProfilesPanel(profiles) — a DOM factory that renders a collapsible panel listing all available profiles. The panel is the primary UI for profile selection.

Implementation:
- Renders a panel element with a list of profile entries
- Entry for each profile in the provided profiles map
- Active entry has aria-current="true"
- Clicking an entry calls setActiveProfile(id) and closes the panel

Keyboard requirements (EDGE-004):
- On open, focus moves to the active profile entry (or first entry if none active)
- Arrow Up/Down navigate between entries
- Enter activates the focused entry (calls setActiveProfile + closes panel)
- Escape closes the panel and restores focus to its prior location

Public API:
- panel.open() — opens and focuses
- panel.close() — closes and restores focus
- panel.element — the root DOM node

Test scenarios (src/profiles-panel.test.js):
- All profiles in PROFILES are listed as entries
- Active profile entry has aria-current="true"
- Clicking an entry calls setActiveProfile with the correct id
- Arrow-key navigation moves focus between entries
- Enter on a focused entry activates it and closes the panel
- Escape closes the panel and restores prior focus
- panel.open() moves focus to the active (or first) entry
close_reason: Added profiles panel tests for listed profiles, aria-current, click activation, focus-on-open, arrow navigation, Enter, and Escape focus restore.

title: Tests: profile switch effects (switch.js)
description:
Write vitest tests covering applyProfileSwitch and reinitProfile behavior.

Test file: src/switch.test.js

Test scenarios for applyProfileSwitch:
- Cell keymaps reinitialize (reinitProfile is called on each cell with the resolved bindings map)
- Session namespace is cleared (window.__clt_session__ is reset)
- Action log is cleared (cell.actionLog.clear() is called)
- If reinitProfile throws, the active profile ID reverts to its prior value

Test scenarios for reinitProfile directly:
- New CM6 EditorView is mounted in the same parent div as the old one
- Document content (text) is preserved across reinitProfile
- A fresh action log is attached after reinitProfile
- Old EditorView is destroyed
close_reason: Added profile switch tests for reinit calls, session reset, action-log clear, rollback, document preservation, fresh log, and old view destruction.

title: Mount fixture in shell.js and register fixture cell in cells array
description:
Update shell.js to register the fixture cell in the cells array so that profile switches reinitialize its keymap alongside the main pane cells.

Changes:
- Call createFixture(container) (which returns the fixture's cell per CLT-c2d)
- Push the returned cell into the cells array: cells.push(fixtureCell)
- This must happen before the first profile change fires (cells is captured by reference
  in the onProfileChange subscription, so adding after subscription setup is safe as long
  as no change fires between setup and push — mount order guarantees this)

Note: 'before the first profile change fires' (not 'before subscribing') — the subscription
is already established by CLT-ye3; this task only adds the cell to the captured array.
close_reason: Mounted fixture in shell.js and registered fixture cell in cells array before profile-change subscription.

Includes one CM6 cell (to verify that cell re-initialization on profile switch coexists with keybinding substitution in the same fixture). Calls renderKeybindings on the section after mount. Returns the created cell.

Subscribes to onProfileChange and re-resolves on each change. renderKeybindings must be idempotent on the same container (guard against duplicate subscriptions).

title: Mount nav-layer, profiles-panel, and which-key overlay in shell.js
description:
Wire the nav layer, profiles panel, and which-key overlay into shell.js after the two-pane layout is created.

Mounting order (after two-pane layout is appended to container):
1. const whichKey = createWhichKey()
2. const panel = createProfilesPanel(PROFILES)
3. installNavLayer(shell, panel, whichKey)

installNavLayer attaches the global keydown listener to the shell element (or window),
using the active profile's leader key to gate interception.

Append any DOM elements (overlay, panel) that need to be in the document to the
shell container before calling installNavLayer.
close_reason: Mounted which-key, profiles panel, and nav layer in shell.js; added shell wiring tests.

title: Create src/nav/nav-layer.js with profile-aware leader key interception
description: Create src/nav/nav-layer.js exporting installNavLayer(shell, panel, whichKey): adds a window-level keydown listener. Reads getActiveProfile() to determine the leader. For non-Space leaders (default/calva/emacs profiles with leader 'g'): applies focus-gate — only intercepts if document.activeElement.closest('.cm-editor') is null. For any profile with leader ' ' (Space, currently vim): checks insert mode on the focused editor via EditorView.findFromDOM before intercepting. On interception, calls whichKey.show([{key:'p', label:'profiles'}]) and wires onKey to route 'p' → panel.open(). After a chord dispatches its action, focus management is the action target's responsibility.
close_reason: Implemented profile-aware nav layer with leader detection, editor focus gate, vim insert-mode gate, which-key hints, and profiles panel routing.

Marks the active profile with aria-current='true'. Subscribes to onProfileChange to update the active marker. Activating an entry calls setActiveProfile(id) and closes the panel. When the panel opens, focus SHALL move to the panel (active or first entry). Supports arrow-key navigation, Enter to activate, Escape to close and restore prior focus.

The overlay is a fixed-position div at the bottom center of the viewport. It registers a one-shot keydown listener on show and cleans up on hide. Calls an optional onKey(key) callback before hiding. The overlay SHALL NOT steal focus.
close_reason: Implemented createWhichKey hint overlay with show/hide, one-shot key listener cleanup, default and per-show onKey callbacks.

title: Update shell.js: maintain cells array and subscribe to profile changes
description:
Update shell.js to maintain a cells array so applyProfileSwitch can reinitialize all active cells on profile change.

Changes:
- Declare a cells = [] array at the top of the shell module
- Wrap each createCell(...) call: const cell = createCell(...); cells.push(cell)
  This covers the two existing pane cells created during Phase 1 layout setup
- Subscribe to onProfileChange: on each change, call applyProfileSwitch(cells, newProfileId)

The cells array must be populated before the subscription fires. Since the subscription
fires only on change (not on init), pushing during createCell calls is safe.

Public: cells is internal — no need to export it.
close_reason: Updated shell.js to maintain cells array and subscribe to profile changes via applyProfileSwitch.

title: Create src/profiles/resolve.js exporting resolveBindings
description: Create src/profiles/resolve.js exporting resolveBindings(profileId): look up profileId in the registry, walk the extends chain, shallow-merge bindings maps with child keys taking precedence (equivalent to Object.assign precedence since all values are strings). Return the flat map. If profileId is unknown, return empty object without throwing. Detect and throw on circular extends chains.
close_reason: Implemented src/profiles/resolve.js with profile lookup, extends-chain merge, unknown-ID empty object, and circular extends detection.

title: Create src/profiles/switch.js exporting applyProfileSwitch
description: Create src/profiles/switch.js exporting applyProfileSwitch(newId, cells): calls resolveBindings(newId) to get a flat bindings map, then for each cell calls cell.reinitProfile(bindings), then calls resetSession(), then clears each cell's new action log. If any effect throws, revert the active profile ID to the prior value and re-throw (atomic switch semantics).
close_reason: Implemented applyProfileSwitch with resolved bindings, cell reinit, session reset, action-log clear, and previous-profile rollback on errors.

title: Create src/profiles/registry.js with PROFILES map

title: Research Calva default Paredit keybindings for CM6 notation
description:
HITL — requires human with browser/VS Code access to verify.

Research the default Paredit keybindings used by Calva (VS Code extension) and express them in CM6 key notation. These will seed the Calva profile's bindings map in calva.js.

Reference: https://github.com/BetterThanTomorrow/calva/blob/dev/src/extension-test/unit/paredit/commands-test.ts and Calva's package.json #contributes.keybindings

Minimum required command keywords (from Phase 1 PROFILE_BINDINGS):
- slurp-forward
- slurp-backward
- barf-forward
- barf-backward
- raise-sexp
- splice-sexp
- split-sexp
- join-sexp

For each: record the default Calva keybinding in CM6 format (e.g., "Ctrl-Right" not "ctrl+right").

Deliverable: A comment block or draft object ready to paste into src/calva.js.
notes: An automated agent cannot safely complete this task — it requires browsing external documentation to avoid fabricating keybindings that would poison all downstream profile tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 0 — Prototype structure-diff fallback (conditional)
description: If action-observation gaps are found in any keymap spike, prototype structure-diff inference as a fallback validation path: before and after each keypress, snapshot the CM6 document; diff the snapshots to infer which structural operation was performed; assess whether the inferred-command set is accurate enough for validation. Only pursue if wrapping coverage is below 95% on a required keymap.
close_reason: Not needed: Phase 0 spikes achieved 100% action-observation coverage for default, vim, and emacs keymap modes; no structure-diff fallback is required.
